title: Living soils
summary: Understand the biological life of the soil (earthworms, fungi, bacteria, humus) and how the permanent bed system naturally feeds your crops.

pages.title: Module overview: the living soil
pages.text: We are going to show you how **growing beds** help keep the **soil alive** to ensure the good health and proper growth of plants and vegetables.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Présentation du module : le sol vivant

pages.title: For a soil to be fertile, it must be alive
pages.text: Let's discover what a soil is made of and why its **biological activity** is essential to fertility.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Pour que le sol soit fertile, il faut qu’il soit vivant

pages.title: The needs of vegetable crops
pages.text:
To grow and stay healthy, vegetable plants need **light**, **water** and **nutrients**.

They feed in the upper layer of the soil (**10 to 20 cm** deep).
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les besoins des plantes maraîchères

pages.title: The humus richness of a fertile soil
pages.text: A fertile soil is rich in **humus**, which comes from **decomposing organic matter** (crop residues, leaves, dead insects, droppings, etc.).
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La richesse en humus d’un sol fertile

pages.title: Humus in the topsoil layer
pages.text: A fertile soil is rich in **humus**, which comes from **decomposing organic matter** (crop residues, leaves, dead insects, droppings, etc.).
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour L’humus dans la couche superficielle du sol

pages.title: The physical composition of the soil
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La composition physique du sol

pages.title: Soil micro-organisms: bacteria and mycelium
pages.text:
The soil is also home to living organisms:

- **micro-organisms** invisible to the naked eye, such as **bacteria** and **fungi** in white filaments, called **mycelium**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les micro-organismes du sol : bactéries et mycélium

pages.title: The mesofauna: mites, nematodes and larvae
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La mésofaune : acariens, nématodes et larves

pages.title: Small soil animals (invertebrates)
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les petits animaux (invertébrés) du sol

pages.title: A rich and diverse ecosystem
pages.text: It is a **very rich and diverse ecosystem** where everyone plays a role, even the slug!
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Un écosystème riche et varié

pages.title: The balance of life in the soil
pages.text: It is a **very rich and diverse ecosystem** where everyone plays a role, even the slug!
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour L’équilibre de la vie dans le sol

pages.title: Biological activity, the engine of fertility
pages.text:
All these elements interact to regenerate the soil, keep it healthy, and keep it **moist, aerated and stable** so that plants can grow.

It is this **biological activity** that drives soil fertility.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour L’activité biologique, moteur de la fertilité

pages.title: How does the growing bed system keep the soil alive?
pages.text: Let's now see how the organization into **permanent growing beds** and **mulched pathways** sustains this biological life and makes the soil fertile.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Comment le système des planches de culture maintient le sol vivant ?

pages.title: Concentrating the fertile soil on the beds
pages.text:
At the start, the plot is covered with a thin layer of fertile soil. When digging the **pathways**, this soil is moved onto the **growing beds**.

This concentrates all the fertile soil exactly where the crops will grow.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Concentrer la terre fertile sur les planches

pages.title: Placing the fertile soil on the beds
pages.text:
At the start, the plot is covered with a thin layer of fertile soil. When digging the **pathways**, this soil is moved onto the **growing beds**.

This concentrates all the fertile soil exactly where the crops will grow.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Mise en place de la terre fertile sur les planches

pages.title: The role of mulch in the pathways
pages.text:
**Mulch** in the pathways is essential:

- It **retains water** like a sponge, keeping the soil moist.
- It **slows down water runoff** during heavy rain, which limits erosion.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle du paillage dans les passe-pieds

pages.title: The role of micro-organisms on the mulch
pages.text: **Micro-organisms** (bacteria and filamentous fungi) feed on the **mulch** laid in the pathways.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle des micro-organismes sur le paillage

pages.title: The soil fauna food chain
pages.text: Micro-organisms are food for **woodlice**, **insects** (termites, ants, etc.), **spiders**, **centipedes**, **millipedes** and **earthworms**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La chaîne alimentaire de la faune du sol

pages.title: The formation of surface compost
pages.text:
All these organisms take part in breaking down the mulch into compost. We can therefore speak of **surface compost** in the pathways.

The droppings and dead bodies of micro-organisms and soil fauna decompose in turn and feed the compost.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La formation du compost de surface

pages.title: Soil aeration through galleries
pages.text: By digging galleries, **earthworms** and **termites** also make it easier for air and water to circulate and help plant roots find their way.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour L’aération du sol grâce aux galeries

pages.title: The release of mineral elements
pages.text: The decomposition of **organic matter** releases **mineral elements** that add to those already present in the soil and are essential for plant growth.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La libération des éléments minéraux

pages.title: Essential mineral elements and trace elements
pages.text:
Each nutrient released into the soil plays a specific role:

- **Nitrogen (N)** promotes leaf development.
- **Phosphorus (P)** promotes root development.
- **Potassium (K)** promotes flower and fruit development.

The soil also supplies **calcium**, **magnesium**, **iron** and other **trace elements**, which are essential for good growth and plant health.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les éléments minéraux et oligo-éléments essentiels

pages.title: How do plants contribute to the soil's biological activity?
pages.text: Plants do not simply draw from the soil: they also feed **biological life** and protect the soil.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Comment les plantes participent à l’activité biologique du sol ?

pages.title: Protecting the soil with foliage
pages.text: Once the plants have grown, they **protect the soil from sun and wind**, thereby limiting drying out and soil degradation.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La protection du sol par le feuillage

pages.title: Photosynthesis feeds soil life
pages.text: The upper part of the plants interacts with light. The **photosynthesis** reaction produces sugar, which then feeds the **fungi** and **bacteria** in the soil.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La photosynthèse nourrit la vie du sol

pages.title: Symbiosis and mycorrhiza
pages.text:
In exchange for the sugar supplied by the plant, some fungi act like a mouth for it: they absorb soil nutrients on its behalf.

This win-win relationship is called a **symbiosis**. When it is established between a plant and a fungus, it is called a **mycorrhiza**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Symbiose et mycorhize

pages.title: The stabilizing role of roots
pages.text:
Plants take advantage of the water and nutrients stored in the **pathways**. To reach them, they extend their root system.

The **roots** stabilize the soil and protect it from erosion and leaching during heavy rains.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle stabilisateur des racines

pages.title: Root decomposition after harvest
pages.text:
After harvest, the roots left in the soil decompose and help enrich the soil with **organic matter**, which feeds the micro-organisms.

In some crops, roots can reach several kilometres in total length: the organic matter they provide as they decompose is therefore far from negligible!
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La décomposition des racines après la récolte

pages.title: Making use of crop residues
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Valoriser les résidus de récolte

pages.title: Applying compost without compacting the soil
pages.text: Before starting a new crop, this **compost** can be spread on the surface without being compacted, so as not to damage the soil structure and to let life organize itself.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Déposer le compost sans tasser le sol

pages.title: Tripling production thanks to living soil
pages.text: The **bio-intensive market gardening on living soil** technique, with permanent beds and mulching, improves soil fertility while **tripling (× 3)** vegetable production compared with conventional methods.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Tripler la production grâce au sol vivant

pages.title: Conclusion: the benefits of growing beds
pages.text: The **growing bed** technique has many advantages: by preserving the soil, it reduces the need for compost and organic matter inputs, and therefore saves **money**, while increasing **productivity** and producing **healthy food**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Conclusion : les bénéfices des planches de culture
